# OPCP Observability - Technical architecture

### Technical Architecture and Stack  
  
**Summary**

  * **Distributed, Compliant Architecture:** We are adopting a scalable Forwarder-Receiver model that pushes edge telemetry to centralized stacks, ensuring the strict multi-tenant network isolation required for SNC compliance.

  * **Two-Tiered Receiver Strategy:** To enforce a strict Control Plane / Data Plane separation, storage and UI are isolated into two distinct boundaries:

    * **Tier 1 (Control Plane):** OPCP Core observability stack for OVHcloud-owned infrastructure operations (IaaS & PaaS).

    * **Tier 2 (Data Plane):** A mandatory Customer Observability App for all tenant workloads.

  * **Mandatory Customer Tier:** The Tier 2 Cloud Store Observability App is mandatory for any OPCP with a Cloud Store. It relies on the native multi-tenancy of Mimir and Loki to strictly separate customer data. The underlying S3 storage for this stack must be provided and paid for by the customer.

  * **Standardized "LGTM" Stack:** All tiers will utilize a unified technical stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir) deployed via GitOps and standardized on industry protocols (OTLP, Prometheus Remote Write).




## **Note:**

**This is a high-level technical architecture for the observability platform(s) for both OPCP and CloudStore / or the whole SOV organization.**

**Technical overview id provided. For functional requirements, refer to the product note:[OPCP - Observability](https://confluence.ovhcloud.tools/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=818640885)**

  


## **Overview**

#### 1\. Technical Architecture & Data Separation

We follow a distributed Forwarder-Receiver model to ensure scalability, flexibility, and SNC compliance. It is fundamentally built on a strict **Control Plane vs. Data Plane separation** :

  * **Control Plane (OVHcloud-owned data):** Telemetry required by OVHcloud to run and operate the OPCP Core and Cloud Store platforms. This data never mixes with customer workloads!

  * **Data Plane (Tenant-owned data):** Telemetry generated by customer workloads (e.g., VMs, Kubernetes, Object Store usage).

    * _Note: If OVHcloud requests its own resources inside the OPCP (e.g., OVH-owned VMs or S3 buckets for management or the cloudstore), OVH acts as a tenant, and this data belongs to the Data Plane._




**Forwarder (Collector Layer)**

  * **Role:** Sits at the edge (Hardware, Network, Hosts, VMs, K8s, Cloud Store apps) to collect and push telemetry.

  * **Components:** * OpenTelemetry (OTel) Collector: Handles ingestion, transformation, and routing of metrics, logs, and future traces.

    * Monitor (Prometheus Agent): Scrapes local targets and performs remote-write to the Receiver.

    * Customer VM probing / LB probing is done here.

  * **Deployment:** Every OPCP component must deploy a stateless forwarder that pipes data to the central stack. We cannot scrape targets FROM controllers due to network restriction.




**Receiver (Storage & UI Layer)**

The receivers are separated into two distinct stacks:

**Tier 1: OPCP Core Observability Stack (The Control Plane)**

  * **Location:** Runs on the OPCP Core controllers (Controller is scalable up to 1 node per rack).

  * **Ingestion:** Collects OVHcloud-owned infrastructure data. This includes Layer 1 hardware, hypervisors, Core control plane, Cloud Store business logic, IAM, catalog health, packaging, see [OPCP - Observability](https://confluence.ovhcloud.tools/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=818640885)

  * **Purpose:** Serves as the operational baseline for OVH to manage both the underlying IaaS platform and the PaaS/Cloud Store platform. Uses best-effort retention to prevent controller storage exhaustion.

  * **Deployment:** On the OPCP core controller K3s cluster (independent of OpenStack).




**Tier 2: Cloud Store Observability App (The Data Plane)**

  * **Location:** Deployed as a **mandatory** application via the CloudStore, running directly in the data plane, like the CloudStore itself.

  * **Ingestion (Data Plane):** Acts as the receiver for all tenant-owned workload telemetry (deployed apps, K8s, Object Storage, VMs). If OVHcloud consumes VMs/S3 natively within OPCP, that telemetry also routes here under an OVH tenant ID.

  * **Multi-Tenancy:** Strictly separates different customers and projects using the native multi-tenancy features of Mimir, Loki, and (later) Tempo.

  * This app just runs as a multi-tenant app in the CloudStore, just as VCF does right now.
  * **Storage & Cost:** The S3 storage backing this stack for long-term retention **must be provided and paid for by the customer**.

  * **Purpose:** Provides Account Admins with a dedicated observability service for long-term retention and high-cardinality exploration without impacting the OVH control planes. It can be queried by a customer-owned observability platform (Zabbix, Datadog, etc.).




#### 2\. Technical Stack Selection

As AGPLv3 has been approved, we will standardize on the industry-standard "LGTM" stack (Option A).

  * **UI:** Grafana (AGPLv3). _(Note: Perses (Apache 2.0) remains an alternative if deeper GitOps/React UI embeddability is required)._

  * **Metrics:** Mimir (AGPLv3) - High performance, S3-native, multi-tenancy enabled.

  * **Logs:** Loki (AGPLv3) - Cost-efficient, uses the same S3 backend as Mimir, multi-tenancy enabled.

  * **Traces:** Tempo (AGPLv3) - Multi-tenancy enabled (planned for future phases).

  * **Storage:** Stores data in S3 (Ceph). _Tier 2 S3 buckets are customer-provided and customer-billed._




#####  Standardized package

  * A standardized observability package will be shared and used for both the OPCP Core controllers and the Cloud Store App to simplify maintenance.
  * Goal: Deploy this Helm chart to OPCP core controller as well as current SNC deployment and package it for the CloudStore → package will be shared, parameters will be diverse across platforms



#### 3\. Standard Protocols & Forwarding

  * **Logs/Traces:** OTLP, or Syslog (RFC 5424/3164) for legacy hardware like Arista switches.

  * **Metrics:** Prometheus Remote Write.

  * **Alert Forwarding:** Webhooks to Arsenal/Opsgenie or customer-owned alert receiving endpoint.

  * **Queries:** PromQL, LogQL (Prometheus/Mimir, Loki).




#### 4\. Management and Deployment

  * Shared package for both observability stack tiers → ensures best maintainability and a unified solution.

  * Owner of each OPCP component must define their own observability rules, based on guidelines (dashboards, alerting, cardinality).

  * Management via GitOps.
